name: Solitaire
description: A star 102 parsecs away, 35 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 72571: radius 34.657 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 310.321 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.093) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 72571: effective temperature 4118 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.043)

gravity.source: SIMBAD's compilation of spectroscopic measurements (mesFe_h): log g 1.33 from 2021MNRAS.505.4496G; the 11 published values span log g 1 to 2, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.1% of the centre brightness

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 72571: distance 101.523 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.07), at which the luminosity and radius hold

text.card: A star 102 parsecs away, 35 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 310 times the Sun's luminosity at 4,118 K, so 34.657 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 72571: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: 58 Hydrae
quotes.card: 58 Hydrae, also named Solitaire, is a single star in the equatorial constellation of Hydra, located around 290 light years away from the Sun based on parallax.
quotes.introduction: It has the Bayer designation E Hydrae; 58 Hydrae is the Flamsteed designation − a later designation of 6 Librae.

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 6219380139469026432 (quality B), from 2006AstL...32..759G; Gaia DR3 measures none
